actions.name: Occurs in at least one protected area

documentation.range: This species is endemic to Taiwan, Province of China (Smith and Xie 2008). It is restricted to elevations below 2,000 m asl (Smith and Xie 2008), becoming common at 1,300 m asl (Yu 1993).
documentation.population: This species has a population density of 2-5 per hectare (Yu and Lin 1999). It is stated to be "common" throughout its range and its population may be stable (Denys et al. 2017).
documentation.habitats: This species occurs in broad-leaf forests and its edge habitat, and scrub (Smith and Xie 2008). Litter size is 2-3 (Yu and Lin 1999). It appears to have specific habitat requirements with dense shrub cover as an important variable (Wang et al. 2008). It is considered an important scatter-hoarder of seeds of species such as Castanopsis indica (Chou and Liao 2024).
documentation.threats: There are no major threats to this species at present. However, human land uses are expected to affect the dispersal of this species (Wang et al. 2008).
documentation.measures: This species is present in Yushan National Park (Yu 1994), but it is not known if it occurs in any other protected areas. In China, this species has been regionally Red Listed as Least Concern (Wang and Xie 2004). Data on its population ecology are lacking.
documentation.rationale: This species is assessed as Least Concern because its extent of occurrence is estimated to be 40,252 km², it has a presumed large population, it occurs in at least one protected area, and because it is unlikely to be declining at nearly the rate required to qualify for listing in a threatened category. Further research of its population would be beneficial.
documentation.taxonomic_notes: This species is sometimes inappropriately referred to as coxingi.
